title: Rav Yehudah bar Chinena

paragraphs: In Bava Kamma 14b, he poses a contradiction to Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua. Hyman also cites Menachot 36a for Rav Yehudah bar Chanina addressing Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua. The parallel in the consulted text is at 46a.

notes.text: Bava Kamma 14b explicitly names Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. The corresponding attribution was not located in the bounded Menachot 36a–b checks; Hyman’s 36a citation is retained as a source question.

The saved whole Davidson Menachot46a paragraph explicitly has Rabbi Yehudah bar Chanina addressing Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua. Supplied Menachot36a is retained alongside the matching46a comparison; no printed ל/מ history is inferred. Hyman’s full Rav title and Chinena/Chanina forms remain, with the named Rabbi form disclosed rather than harmonized. רמי is read as posing a contradiction in the supplied Bava Kamma clause, not a new speaker named Rami; the earlier bounded Bava check is not a new inspection here.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 562) gives Menachot 36a and the title Rav. The inspected Menachot 46a names Rabbi Yehudah bar Chanina and gives the same addressee. Bava Kamma 14b names Rav Yehudah bar Chinena and explicitly makes him the one who raises the contradiction.
